solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Showing surprise on the square perhaps, deny a lie that's false

parts.note: a batter at the crease on a cricket square is batting; 'perhaps' marks this as one example

indicators.note: a false version of the words is a faked rearrangement of their letters

explanation.surface: Someone shows surprise while denying a lie that turns out to be untrue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's false' rearranges DENYALIE into ANEYELID. The square is the cricket square, the central strip of a cricket field where the batting takes place.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom not batting an eyelid means staying calm, so its positive form describes visible astonishment.

clue.text: What's said to be famous dandy's remains

indicators.note: what is said is what is spoken, so the words that follow are heard rather than spelt

parts.note: Beau Nash was the celebrated eighteenth-century dandy and master of ceremonies at Bath

explanation.surface: A question about what a celebrated fop left behind after death.
explanation.walkthrough: Beau Nash, the Georgian leader of fashion at Bath, is said aloud to give the two words of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Bone ash is the white residue left when bones are burnt, so it is literally remains.

clue.text: Try to persuade office worker to be on time

parts.note: a temp is a temporary office worker

explanation.surface: Encouraging a temporary employee to turn up punctually.
explanation.definitionFit: To tempt someone is to try to persuade or entice them into doing something.

clue.text: Litmus perhaps in acid turned to red at first

indicators.note: turned means the letters of acid are twisted into a new order
at first takes only the opening letter of red

explanation.surface: Litmus paper dipped in acid turns red at the start of an experiment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' makes DICA from ACID; 'at first' gives R from red.
explanation.definitionFit: Litmus is an example of a chemical indicator that changes colour to show acidity.

clue.text: Encourages keeping company holding thousand exotic pets

indicators.note: keeping means one piece holds another within it

parts.note: gees, as in gees up, means encourages

indicators.note: holding means the second piece is gripped inside the first

explanation.surface: Someone urges a firm that holds a thousand unusual animals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' and 'keeping' nest the pieces: the thousand sits inside the company, and that sits inside the encouraging word, as in gees up a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Geckos are small lizards often kept as unusual household pets.

clue.text: Need law to be changed for US Government programme

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are changed into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A call for legislation to be reformed by the American government.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be changed' rearranges NEEDLAW.
explanation.definitionFit: Roosevelt's New Deal was the 1930s American federal programme of economic recovery.

clue.text: Shouts lines in agreement

indicators.note: in places one piece within another

parts.note: yes is a word of agreement
L is an abbreviation for line, doubled for lines

explanation.surface: People shout lines in unison as they agree.
explanation.definitionFit: To yell is to shout loudly; the plural verb forms match.

clue.text: Most stupid of Americans anyhow

definitions.meaning: ... means the opposite of wisest, hence most foolish
an American colloquial word meaning at any rate or anyway

explanation.walkthrough: Read as two words the answer means most stupid; as one it is a US colloquialism for anyway.
explanation.definitionFit: Least wise literally means having the least wisdom, while the joined form is American dialect for at any rate.

clue.text: Any gold changed for 24 hours

indicators.note: changed means the letters are put into a different order

explanation.surface: Some gold is exchanged for a day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changed' rearranges ANYGOLD.
explanation.definitionFit: Something daylong lasts throughout the whole day, all twenty-four hours of it.

clue.text: Having domain unsettled, getting about

indicators.note: unsettled means the letters of domain are disturbed into a new order

parts.note: C, for circa, is the abbreviation for about

explanation.surface: Someone whose territory is unsettled moves around from place to place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unsettled' rearranges DOMAIN into NOMADI. The whole clue also describes a wanderer with no fixed territory.
explanation.definitionFit: A nomadic people roam about without a settled home territory, as the whole clue describes.

clue.text: Foolish chap bagging a black jumper

indicators.note: bagging means putting something in a bag, so one piece encloses another

parts.note: a wally is British slang for a silly man
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A silly man pockets a black sweater.
explanation.walkthrough: WALLY is British slang for a fool. 'jumper' looks like a sweater, as it is in Britain, but here it means an animal that leaps.
explanation.definitionFit: A wallaby is a small kangaroo-like marsupial that moves by jumping.

clue.text: Vegetable garden containing kale initially put on large lorry

indicators.note: put on means the following piece sits next to the earlier one in the entry

parts.note: an artic is an articulated lorry, a large British truck

indicators.note: containing means the first piece holds the next within it

parts.note: to hoe is to work a garden with a hoe

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of kale

explanation.surface: Vegetables from a garden, including kale, are loaded onto a big truck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' gives K, and 'containing' puts it inside HOE. An artic is British for an articulated lorry, a large truck.
explanation.definitionFit: The globe artichoke is a vegetable whose flower bud is eaten.

clue.text: Where you'll see badgers getting over fight

parts.note: a sett is the burrow where badgers live
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: Badgers come out of their home to have a fight.
explanation.definitionFit: A set-to is a brief fight or heated argument.

clue.text: Suit husband going in cosy places

indicators.note: going in means one piece is put inside another

parts.note: hearts is one of the four suits of cards

explanation.surface: A husband makes himself comfortable at home in a suit.
explanation.definitionFit: The hearth, the floor of a fireplace, stands for warm and homely places.

clue.text: Humiliation in a cellar?

parts.note: a basement is a cellar below a house

explanation.surface: Being humiliated by being sent to a cellar.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits that the answer is read as two words, 'a' plus a cellar.
explanation.definitionFit: Abasement means being degraded or humiliated, brought low in dignity.

clue.text: Author of Eyeless in Gaza

indicators.note: of means letters taken out of the words that follow

explanation.surface: Asking who wrote the novel Eyeless in Gaza.
explanation.walkthrough: Eyeless in Gaza is actually Aldous Huxley's novel, which tempts a solver toward Huxley; but the author sits inside the title.
explanation.definitionFit: Doris Lessing was a Nobel Prize-winning British novelist, so she is an author.

clue.text: Sign of penitence to fire clergymen generally

parts.note: to sack someone is to fire them from a job
the cloth is a collective term for the clergy

explanation.surface: Dismissing clergymen as a sign of repentance.
explanation.definitionFit: Wearing sackcloth was a traditional biblical mark of mourning and repentance.

clue.text: Several connected things taking in King George to cause annoyance

indicators.note: taking in means one piece swallows another

parts.note: a chain is a series of connected links or items
GR stands for Georgius Rex, King George

explanation.surface: A string of events involving King George annoys people.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as a verb, the word means to vex or mortify, which is to cause annoyance.

clue.text: Man that's cut about the ear gets disorganised

indicators.note: cut means its last letter is cut off

parts.note: a chap is a man
otic is the adjective relating to the ear

explanation.surface: A man with an injury near his ear becomes confused.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's cut' removes the last letter P from CHAP, leaving CHA.
explanation.definitionFit: Something chaotic is in total confusion, completely disorganised.

clue.text: Useless competitor — taking on rising pro he got smashed

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the word on is read upwards
smashed means the letters of pro he are broken and reassembled

explanation.surface: A hopeless rival takes on a professional, who then gets drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns ON into NO; 'got smashed' rearranges PROHE into HOPER. 'smashed' suggests drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: A no-hoper is someone with no chance of success, such as a hopeless competitor.

clue.text: Weapon guerrilla leader stuck in fellow

indicators.note: stuck in means one piece is pushed inside another

parts.note: a mate is a fellow or companion
Che Guevara was the famous guerrilla leader

explanation.surface: A rebel leader's weapon is stuck into his comrade.
explanation.definitionFit: A machete is a broad heavy knife that can be used as a weapon.

clue.text: Person is standing up on seat

parts.note: a man is a person

indicators.note: standing up in a down clue means the word is is read upwards

explanation.surface: Someone is standing on a chair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'standing up' turns IS into SI. 'seat' means a country seat, not a chair.
explanation.definitionFit: A country seat is a large house belonging to a landed family, such as a grand residence.

clue.text: Distillation made by member of religious community around Chartreuse primarily

indicators.note: around means the first piece wraps the second

parts.note: an Essene was a member of an ancient Jewish ascetic community

indicators.note: primarily takes the first letter of Chartreuse

explanation.surface: Monks distil the spirit of Chartreuse liqueur.
explanation.walkthrough: 'primarily' gives C, which goes inside ESSENE. Chartreuse is a liqueur made by monks, fitting the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: An essence is a concentrated extract obtained by distilling a substance.

clue.text: Soldier perhaps infiltrated by good English spy

indicators.note: infiltrated by means the first piece has others put into it

parts.note: a soldier ant is one kind of ant

explanation.surface: A soldier's unit is infiltrated by a good English spy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soldier' suggests an army man, but it is a soldier ant.
explanation.definitionFit: An agent is a spy working secretly for a government.

clue.text: Slope on hard cultivated land

parts.note: a tilt is a slope or slant
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A slope over hard farmland.
explanation.definitionFit: Tilth is soil that has been tilled, so it is land under cultivation.

clue.text: A northern detective in bad mood's restraining device

indicators.note: in means those pieces are placed inside another

parts.note: a huff is a bad mood; the possessive gives a final S
DC is a Detective Constable

explanation.surface: A grumpy northern detective's handcuffs.
explanation.walkthrough: DC stands for Detective Constable, a British police rank.
explanation.definitionFit: Handcuffs are a pair of linked metal rings used to restrain a prisoner's wrists.

clue.text: Father holding Australian bird's bone

indicators.note: holding means the first piece holds the second within it

parts.note: FR is the abbreviation for Father, a priest's title
the emu is a large flightless Australian bird

explanation.surface: A priest holding a bird's bone.
explanation.definitionFit: The femur is the thigh bone, the longest in the body.

clue.text: Ascot may be gripped by this closest of races with fast pace

definitions.text: Ascot may be gripped by this

parts.note: a tie, or dead heat, is the closest possible finish of a race
clip means a fast pace, as in at a good clip

explanation.surface: Ascot racecourse hosts the closest finish, run at a fast pace.
explanation.walkthrough: Ascot is a famous English racecourse, which 'races' supports, but here an ascot is a broad cravat.
explanation.definitionFit: A tie clip fastens a tie or cravat, and an ascot is a broad neckcloth.

clue.text: Powerful chap, one such as Hadrian pressing North

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: pressing means one piece is pressed into the other

parts.note: Emperor Hadrian was a Roman

explanation.surface: A strong man, perhaps Emperor Hadrian, presses north with his wall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pressing' puts N inside ROMAN. Hadrian built his wall across the north of England.
explanation.definitionFit: An iron man is a man of great strength and stamina.

clue.text: Book unravelling ethnic treachery

indicators.note: unravelling means the letters are untangled into a new order

explanation.surface: A book exposes ethnic betrayal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unravelling' rearranges ETHNICTREACHERY.
explanation.definitionFit: Salinger's novel of teenage alienation is a famous book.
